The predictive performance of tree based machine learning methods, in general, improves with a decreasing rate as the size of training data increases.

arxiv-2107-01633.description: Abstract Context. Observations of the redshifted 21-cm line of neutral hydrogen (H i ) are a new and powerful window of observation that offers us the possibility to map the spatial distribution of cosmic H i and learn about cosmology.

arxiv-2203-12595.title: PhysioMTL: Personalizing Physiological Patterns using Optimal Transport Multi-Task Regression Work done while at Apple.
arxiv-2203-12595.creator: Jiacheng Zhu ‡ \ddagger, Gregory Darnell † \dagger, Agni Kumar † \dagger, Ding Zhao ‡ \ddagger, Bo Li § \mathsection, Xuanlong Nguyen ¶ \mathparagraph, Shirley You Ren † \dagger
arxiv-2203-12595.description: Abstract Heart rate variability (HRV) is a practical and noninvasive measure of autonomic nervous system activity, which plays an essential role in cardiovascular health. However, using HRV to assess physiology status is challenging. Even in clinical settings, HRV is sensitive to acute stressors such as physical activity, mental stress, hydration, alcohol, and sleep.

arxiv-2304-09180.title: clotFoam: An Open-Source Framework to Simulate Blood Clot Formation Under Arterial Flow Journal: SoftwareX
arxiv-2304-09180.creator: David Montgomery, Federico Municchi, Karin Leiderman
arxiv-2304-09180.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by David Montgomery, Federico Municchi, Karin Leiderman. Blood clotting involves the coupled processes of platelet aggregation and coagulation. Simulating clotting under flow in complex geometries is challenging due to multiple temporal and spatial scales and high computational cost. clotFoam is an open-source software developed in OpenFOAM that employs a continuum model of platelet advection, diffusion, and aggregation in a dynamic fluid environment and a simplified coagulation model with proteins that advect, diffuse, and react within the fluid and with wall-bound species through reactive boundary conditions.

arxiv-2305-16952.title: The influence of planetesimal fragmentation on planet formation
arxiv-2305-16952.creator: Nicolas Kaufmann, Yann Alibert
arxiv-2305-16952.description: Abstract Context. The effects of planetesimal fragmentation on planet formation has been studied by various models on single embryos therefore neglecting concurrent effects mostly in the outer disk. They show that planetesimal fragmentation can both hinder or aid planet formation due to the introduction of competing effects, namely speeding up accretion and depleting the feeding zone of forming planets. Aims.

arxiv-2306-02662.title: Fully Dynamic All-Pairs Shortest Paths: Likely Optimal Worst-Case Update Time
arxiv-2306-02662.creator: Xiao Mao
arxiv-2306-02662.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Xiao Mao. The All-Pairs Shortest Paths (APSP) problem is one of the fundamental problems in theoretical computer science. It asks to compute the distance matrix of a given n n -vertex graph. We revisit the classical problem of maintaining the distance matrix under a fully dynamic setting undergoing vertex insertions and deletions with a fast worst-case running time and efficient space usage.

arxiv-2312-05185.title: AI Competitions and Benchmarks: Competition platforms
arxiv-2312-05185.creator: \name Andrey Ustyuzhanin \email andrey.u@gmail.com, \name Harald Carlens \email harald@mlcontests.com
arxiv-2312-05185.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by \name Andrey Ustyuzhanin \email andrey.u@gmail.com, \name Harald Carlens \email harald@mlcontests.com. The ecosystem of artificial intelligence competitions is a diverse and multifaceted landscape, encompassing a variety of platforms that each host numerous competitions annually, alongside a plethora of specialized websites dedicated to singular contests. These platforms adeptly manage the overarching administrative responsibilities inherent in orchestrating competitions, thus affording organizers the liberty to allocate greater attention to other facets of their contests.

arxiv-2505-04531.title: Overcoming Data Scarcity in Generative Language Modelling for Low-Resource Languages: A Systematic Review
arxiv-2505-04531.creator: Josh McGiff, Nikola S. Nikolov
arxiv-2505-04531.description: Abstract . Generative language modelling has surged in popularity with the emergence of services such as ChatGPT and Google Gemini. While these models have demonstrated transformative potential in productivity and communication, they overwhelmingly cater to high-resource languages like English. This has amplified concerns over linguistic inequality in natural language processing (NLP).

arxiv-2505-18383.title: NileChat: Towards Linguistically Diverse and Culturally Aware LLMs for Local Communities
arxiv-2505-18383.creator: Abdellah El Mekki Houdaifa Atou Omer Nacar, Shady Shehata Muhammad Abdul-Mageed
arxiv-2505-18383.description: Abstract Enhancing the linguistic capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) to include low-resource languages is a critical research area. Current research directions predominantly rely on synthetic data generated by translating English corpora, which, while demonstrating promising linguistic understanding and translation abilities, often results in models aligned with source language culture.

arxiv-2510-13726.title: Efficient Wall-Modelled Large Eddy Simulation of Rotors using Homogenized Lattice Boltzmann Methods
arxiv-2510-13726.creator: Adrian Kummerländer, Shota Ito, Maximilian Schecher, Davide Dapelo, Stephan Simonis, Mathias J. Krause, Fedor Bukreev
arxiv-2510-13726.description: Abstract Accurately capturing the dynamic forces acting on rotors as well as their wake effects presents a significant challenge for computational fluid dynamics (CFD) due to high Reynolds numbers and a large range of spatio-temporal scales. The present work proposes a novel blade-resolved wall-modeled large eddy simulation (WMLES) approach based on the lattice Boltzmann method (LBM).

arxiv-2512-07549.title: An Infinite Transitivity Theorem
arxiv-2512-07549.creator: Miles Gould
arxiv-2512-07549.description: Abstract . In this note, we promote an infinite Kadison transitivity theorem on massive C ∗ C^{*} -algebras, including the Calkin algebra. This transitivity stems from the analog of countable degree-1 saturation on pure states which is inherited from these algebras via excision.

pmc-12863383.title: Presencia de Aedes aegypti en una zona alta en Bolivia
pmc-12863383.creator: César Rios-Escalier, Ninoska Rosas-Díaz, María de los Ángeles Delgadillo-Iglesias, María Teresa Solís-Soto
pmc-12863383.description: ResumenIntroducciónAedes aegypti es un vector de patógenos arbovirales que causa, anualmente, cientos de millones de casos de dengue, fiebre amarilla, Zika y Chikungunya y está ampliamente distribuido a nivel mundial. Aunque estos mosquitos habitan comúnmente en zonas tropicales y subtropicales a bajas altitudes, estudios recientes los han encontrado hasta a 2.500 metros sobre el nivel del mar (msnm).

pmc-12977990.title: Clinical Characteristics and Risk Factors of Exogenous Insulin Antibody Syndrome in Patients with Diabetes: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-12977990.creator: Jing Zhou, Jiajun Li, Ziyue Wang, Xulei Dai, Nenghan Zhang, Lingqi Kong, Siyuan Wu, Jiangyan Liu, Yan Zhang, Tuo Han
pmc-12977990.description: BackgroundInsulin autoimmune syndrome (IAS) is a rare hypoglycemic disorder often confused with insulinoma or insulin overdose. Patients with diabetes on insulin therapy increasingly show insulin autoantibodies (IAAs), presenting symptoms similar to classic IAS, termed exogenous insulin antibody syndrome (EIAS). This study examines EIAS clinical features and risk factors.

pmc-13272922.description: BackgroundMaintaining activities of daily living is of great importance for patients who have cancer, and dependency is associated with psychological distress.
